# Pesher Habakkuk Column 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QpHab (Cave 1), Col. 1 | **Condition:** Upper portion heavily damaged; lower lines better preserved

---

**1:1** [...The bur]den received by Habakkuk the prophet [in a vision...]

**1:2** [...] How long, LORD, must I call for help and You refuse to listen? I shout to You, "Violence!" yet You do not rescue.

**1:3** Why do You force me to witness evil and make me look at injustice? Ruin and violence surround me; there is conflict and strife everywhere [...]

**1:4** [This passage refers to...] those who proved faithless along with the Man of the Lie, for they refused to [listen to] the Teacher of Righteousness, who spoke from God's own mouth.

**1:5** It also [concerns] those who broke faith with the new [covenant,] because they refused to trust God's covenant [and desecrated] His holy name.

**1:6** In the same way, this passage applies to the faith[less] in the last days.

**1:7** These are the violent ones of the covenant who will refuse to believe

**1:8** when they hear everything that will happen to the final generation,

**1:9** as told by the priest into whose heart

**1:10** God placed insight to explain all the words of His servants the prophets,

**1:11** [through] whom God announced everything that would happen to His people and [His] community.

**1:12** "The law is paralyzed and justice never prevails;

**1:13** the wicked hem in the righteous" (Hab 1:4).

**1:14** [The meaning:] the wicked one is the Wicked Priest, and the righteous one

**1:15** is the Teacher of Righteousness [...]

**1:16** "Look at the nations and watch —

**1:17** be utterly amazed and astonished [...]" (Hab 1:5)

---
*PNEUMA notes: Column 1 covers Hab 1:1-5. This translation prioritizes clarity and natural English while preserving the pesher's interpretive structure. The commentary applies Habakkuk's ancient prophecy to the Qumran sect's own conflicts and expectations. Key figures retained as titles: Teacher of Righteousness, Wicked Priest, Man of the Lie, Kittim (Romans), Spouter of Lies. [...] marks genuine gaps in the manuscript.*
